title: Priya Traders v. Mehta Enterprises
full_text: FACTS: Priya Traders supplied goods to Mehta Enterprises on credit. Mehta Enterprises issued a post-dated cheque for Rs. 2,10,000 towards the outstanding balance. The cheque was dishonoured due to 'account closed'. The complainant issued a demand notice within the statutory 30-day window, which was duly served, but the accused failed to make payment within 15 days of receipt. ISSUE: Whether dishonour on the ground of 'account closed' falls within the scope of Section 138, and whether the accused's defence that the debt was time-barred under the Limitation Act could defeat the presumption under Section 139. REASONING: The court held that the expression 'insufficiency of funds' in Section 138 has been interpreted broadly by the Supreme Court to include dishonour for reasons such as 'account closed', 'stop payment', and 'account frozen', so long as the cheque was issued for a legally enforceable debt at the time of issuance. On the limitation defence, the court noted that a time-barred debt cannot be the basis of a legally enforceable debt for the purposes of Section 138, but placed the burden on the accused to first raise probable evidence rebutting the Section 139 presumption before the limitation defence could be considered. HOLDING: Since the accused failed to lead any evidence to rebut the presumption of a legally enforceable debt, the conviction under Section 138 was upheld. The court awarded compensation equal to the cheque amount plus interest at 9% per annum from the date of dishonour.
